text:
Logan Cooley has 22 points in 19 games, and the part that jumps out is where they come from: 15 on the power play. In his last ten he has 14 points, 10 of them goals, including three-goal nights in Pittsburgh and Montreal, where we'd expect about 10 points at his ice time.

Our numbers call the run earned and inflated at once. Earned, because the chances grew: 4.5 expected goals (the quality of his shots) in those ten games against 3.5 usual. Inflated, because 11 goals on 6.3 expected means shooting 35%, against 24% last season. The chances are real; that finishing rate rarely lasts, so he's flagged as due to cool.

The style should travel. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries and creating 8.4 primary shot assists per 60, 85th percentile among forwards. Only 16 players have added more wins with their goals this season, by our count.

He returned against Vancouver on Nov. 16 after missing games and picked up an assist in 23.8 minutes. That workload is the thing to watch for Utah now.
